cards.say: A strong prompt tells the model **what to do, for whom, and what a good result looks like**.
points: Format: how the answer should look

cards.q: Which prompt is most likely to get a useful answer?
options: Write a friendly 3-sentence blurb on our app for IT managers, with a call to action.
cards.why: It names the task, audience, length, tone and ending, so the model has far less to guess.

cards.q: Match each prompt part to its job
pairs: Sets the point of view, like an editor
Adds background the model can't guess
Says how the answer should look
cards.why: You don't need all four every time, but each one removes guesswork.

cards.before: Giving one or two examples of what you want is called
cards.why: Few-shot prompting shows the model examples of the pattern to follow.

cards.q: Tap the habit that usually hurts results.
sentences: Say who the answer is for.
Pack five unrelated tasks into one message.
cards.why: One clear task per prompt is easier to follow. Split big jobs into steps.

cards.q: Improve a weak answer, in order
steps: Read what the model got wrong
Add the missing context to your prompt
cards.why: Prompting is iterative: change one thing, compare, and keep what works.
